speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context; given your history of diabetes and outdoor activities, could you describe the specific appearance, color, and texture of the rash on the back of your left hand, and have you noticed any pain, itching, or blistering?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis

The description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a 65-year-old with a history of sun exposure is highly suggestive of Actinic Keratosis, a precancerous skin lesion caused by chronic UV damage. Given the lack of pain or tenderness, this aligns well with the typical presentation, but I need to confirm if there are any changes in size, color, or bleeding.

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of left dorsal hand lesion.

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
